html:
Electoral Hesse was a German state centred on Kassel, the old Landgraviate of Hesse-Kassel, whose ruler was raised to the rank of Elector of the Holy Roman Empire in 1803. When the Empire ended three years later he kept the title, though there was no emperor left to elect.

The landgraves had grown rich by hiring out their soldiers. The Hessians who fought for Britain in the American Revolutionary War came mostly from here. In 1807 Napoleon swallowed the state into the Kingdom of Westphalia, ruled by his brother Jérôme. Elector William I came back in 1813 and tried to undo every reform.

Its rulers were stubborn and unpopular, and its constitution was a constant fight. The Brothers Grimm worked in Kassel and gathered many of their tales in the region. Electoral Hesse sided with Austria in 1866, and Prussia annexed it after the Austro-Prussian War.
